label: Earlier G6 benchmark study, audited, not re-validated
about: G6's earlier per-component benchmark studies (April to June 2026), with the figures the 2026 audits corrected them to. None has been re-run on the open-source library; the ones marked as candidates are to be re-run as registered studies.

rows.what_g6_did: MCP tools: grounding, web search, retrieval, planning
rows.audit: Sound on audit, but G6 had twice the baseline's budget.
rows.in_library: partly: g6.mcp, g6.grounding, g6.navigator; no web search
rows.note: Sound on audit; G6 had twice the baseline's budget.

rows.what_g6_did: MCP tools: grounding, web search, retrieval
rows.audit: Sound on audit; not significant (p 0.065), and G6 had twice the budget.
rows.in_library: partly: g6.mcp, g6.grounding; no web search
rows.note: Sound on audit; G6 had twice the budget, and on its own it falls just short of significance (p 0.065).

rows.what_g6_did: Planning and reasoning architectures with a computer-algebra system
rows.audit: The numbers held, but a later audit found one credited tool (SOAR) returns a constant, so which part helped is unproven.
rows.in_library: no: GPS and SOAR were not ported; g6.formal has Z3 only
rows.note: The numbers held; which tool made the gain is unproven.

rows.what_g6_did: Theory building from past attempts, with G6's tools
rows.audit: Sound at matched effort (p 0.0074). The page led with 47%, which came from re-solving only G6's arm.

rows.what_g6_did: A safety gate with a model harm judge
rows.audit: It measured refusing harmful prompts, not blocking actions, and stopped 25% of harmless ones.
rows.note: It measured refusing harmful prompts, not blocking actions, and also stopped 25% of harmless ones.

rows.audit: The gain was coverage: the baseline skipped 34 overlong items. On the 61 both answered, the baseline won 39 to 28.
rows.note: The gain is coverage: G6 answered the 34 overlong items the model alone skipped; on the items both answered, the model alone did better.

rows.what_g6_did: Grounding, debate, retrieval and a computer-algebra system
rows.audit: Not significant (p 0.18). An earlier +8.4 points came from a chosen subset and was withdrawn.

rows.what_g6_did: Formal solvers and Z3 for the tractable subtasks
rows.audit: Not significant (p 0.125). An earlier 95% was found to be partly fabricated and was withdrawn; the debate tool it used was a mock.

rows.what_g6_did: Retrieval from a medical corpus, with elimination prompting
rows.audit: Not significant (p 0.135), and its corpus came from textbooks whose licences were never cleared.
rows.in_library: partly: g6.grounding with your own corpus
rows.note: Not significant on its own (p 0.135); the corpus's licences were never cleared.

rows.what_g6_did: Eighteen job agents, scored by a rubric judge
rows.audit: An earlier "18 of 18 agents at 70% or more" was misleading: 2 of 18 reached it, and a model judge scored it.
rows.in_library: no: the job agents are not ported
rows.note: Scored by a model judge; 2 of the 18 job agents reached 70%.

rows.audit: A +46-point gain was withdrawn: there was no paired baseline run.
rows.note: No paired baseline was run, so the gain cannot be measured.

rows.audit: A 0% to 70.2% gain was withdrawn: it trained on the evaluation questions. Only the clean baseline remains.
rows.specialised: 70.2% on the questions it trained on
rows.note: Trained on the evaluation questions themselves: specialisation, not held-out accuracy. A held-out study is next.

rows.audit: An earlier 81 of 183 replayed strategies built on the test games. Live, G6 equalled random play.
rows.specialised: 44% (81 of 183) with strategies built on these games
rows.note: The strategies were built on these same games; played fresh, G6 matched random play (6 of 183).

rows.audit: No difference: the baseline was already near the ceiling.
rows.note: The model alone was already near the ceiling.
Both near the ceiling, on 16 of 25 tasks.

rows.what_g6_did: Computational tools, with task classifiers in one arm
rows.audit: No gain: both arms already had the skills.
rows.note: Both arms already had the skills.
